disclaimer: Offline emergency medical and crisis precaution guidelines verified by standard disaster civil defence protocols. Designed for immediate field application without internet connectivity.

precautions.summary: Rapid water level rise, breached drainage canals, and contaminated floodwaters.
dos: Move to the highest floor or elevated roof structure immediately.
Turn off the main electrical breaker and LPG gas cylinder valves before water reaches switches.
Probe water depth and hidden manholes with a sturdy walking stick before taking any step.
Store drinking water in sealed bottles on top shelves.
Keep emergency ID, passport, medicines, and phone in double ziplock waterproof bags.
donts: DO NOT walk into moving floodwater deeper than 6 inches (sweeps adults off balance).
DO NOT drive a vehicle into submerged underpasses (vehicles float in 12-18 inches).
DO NOT touch metal railings, lamp posts, or wet walls near electrical meters.
DO NOT drink standing tap water or floodwater under any circumstances.

precautions.summary: Sustained winds >90 km/h, uprooted trees, detached tin sheets, and structural impacts.
dos: Take shelter in an interior windowless hallway, stairwell, or reinforced bathroom.
Secure or tape large glass panels and close all heavy curtains to catch flying glass.
Charge power banks, mobile phones, and emergency flashlights before landfall.
Keep a battery-operated radio or StreetVerism app ready for civil updates.
donts: DO NOT go outside during the calm 'eye' of the storm; ferocious winds return suddenly from the reverse direction.
DO NOT stand near glass windows, sliding doors, or skylights.
DO NOT park vehicles under large trees, old billboards, or temporary tin roofs.

precautions.summary: Submerged transformers, snapped high-voltage cables, and charged standing water.
dos: Assume every dangling or submerged wire is live, energized, and lethal.
Maintain a minimum distance of at least 10 meters (33 feet) from any fallen wire.
If you feel an electric tingling in your feet, hop away with both feet glued together or shuffle without lifting your feet.
Report sparking transformers to local civil defence personnel immediately.
donts: DO NOT touch any person who is in contact with a live electrical current with your bare hands.
DO NOT walk through standing water that has fallen cables touching it anywhere within 50 meters.
DO NOT use corded electrical equipment or plug in wet phone chargers.

precautions.summary: Sewage overflow, leptospirosis, cholera, and vector-borne infection risks.
dos: Boil all water vigorously for at least 3 minutes before drinking or cooking.
Use chlorine purification tablets (1 tablet per 20 liters) if boiling is impossible.
Wash feet and hands thoroughly with soap or antiseptic Dettol after any floodwater contact.
Wear enclosed waterproof footwear or wrap plastic over shoes if forced to wade.
donts: DO NOT eat open food or fruits that came in contact with floodwater.
DO NOT allow children to play or swim in floodwater.
DO NOT ignore minor cuts or abrasions; disinfect and bandage them immediately to prevent leptospirosis.

steps: SAFE RESCUE: Pull victim from water to dry, stable ground. Do not put yourself in danger of drowning.
CHECK RESPONSE: Tap victim firmly on collarbone and shout loudly: 'Are you OK? Can you hear me?'
CALL FOR HELP: Shout loudly for emergency medical services (dial 108 or 112).
CHECK BREATHING: Look at chest and listen for breathing for 10 seconds. If not breathing or only gasping:
HAND PLACEMENT: Place the heel of one hand in the center of the victim's chest (between nipples). Place other hand on top and interlock fingers.
CHEST COMPRESSIONS: Lock elbows straight. Push hard and fast at 100 to 120 beats per minute (depth: 5-6 cm). Allow chest to completely rise between each compression.
CONTINUOUS: Do not stop compressions until the victim coughs/breathes or professional medics arrive.
warnings: DO NOT waste time trying to drain water from lungs with abdominal pushes; start CPR compressions immediately.
DO NOT stop chest compressions for more than 10 seconds.

steps: DIRECT PRESSURE: Press a clean, thick cloth, folded towel, or shirt directly against the bleeding wound.
CONTINUOUS HOLD: Press firmly with both hands without lifting the cloth for at least 10 unbroken minutes.
ADD LAYERS: If blood soaks through, DO NOT remove the first cloth (it breaks developing blood clots). Add a second thick cloth over it and press harder.
ELEVATE: Raise the bleeding limb above heart level (only if no broken bones are suspected).

TOURNIQUET (LAST RESORT): If bright red blood is spurting from an arm or leg and cannot be stopped, wrap a wide belt or cloth strip 2-3 inches above the wound. Twist with a stick until bleeding stops. Mark exact time on victim's forehead.
warnings: DO NOT lift the cloth to 'peek' at the wound during the first 10 minutes.
DO NOT apply a tourniquet over a joint (elbow or knee).

steps: IMMOBILIZE: Keep the injured limb in the exact position it was found. Do NOT attempt to straighten or force the bone.
SUPPORT SPLINT: Place rigid materials (thick wooden sticks, rolled newspapers, umbrellas, or folded cardboard) along both sides of the injured limb.
SECURE SPLINT: Tie strips of cloth or bandages above and below the fracture site. Ensure the joints both above and below the break are stabilized.
CHECK CIRCULATION: Gently press a fingernail or toenail on the splinted limb. It should turn pink within 2 seconds. If it stays pale or cold, loosen the ties slightly.
COLD COMPRESS: Apply a cold pack or cloth soaked in cold rainwater wrapped in plastic around the area to reduce swelling.
warnings: DO NOT attempt to push an exposed broken bone back beneath the skin.
DO NOT give the victim food or water if surgery might be required shortly.

steps: DRY ENVIRONMENT: Move victim out of water, rain, and cold winds into a covered shelter immediately.
STRIP WET CLOTHES: Gently peel off cold, soaked clothing. Do not roughly shake the victim.
CORE WARMING: Wrap victim in dry blankets, towels, or emergency silver thermal foil. Cover the head (leaves face exposed).
WARM LIQUIDS: If fully conscious, provide warm sweet tea or warm sugar water in small sips.
BODY HEAT: Place warm dry cloths or warm water bottles wrapped in cloth against the chest, neck, and armpits.
warnings: DO NOT rub or massage the victim's arms or legs (can force cold blood into heart and trigger fatal arrest).
DO NOT give alcohol or coffee.

steps: DISCONNECT SOURCE: Do NOT touch the victim directly. Turn off circuit breaker or push wire away using a dry non-conductive object (wooden broom handle or dry rope).
CHECK ABCs: Check Airway, Breathing, and Circulation. Begin CPR immediately if victim is unresponsive.
COOL BURNS: Gently pour clean bottled water over entry and exit burns for 10-15 minutes.
COVER BURNS: Cover burned areas with a clean, dry, lint-free cloth or sterile gauze. Keep victim lying down with feet elevated slightly to combat shock.
warnings: DO NOT touch victim with bare hands or wet materials while they are still in contact with power.
DO NOT pop burn blisters or apply butter, oil, or ointments.

steps: CALM VICTIM: Keep the person completely calm and still. Panic increases heart rate and pumps venom faster through bloodstream.
IMMOBILIZE LIMB: Keep the bitten limb completely immobilized and positioned BELOW the level of the heart.
REMOVE CONSTRICTIONS: Quickly remove rings, bracelets, watches, and tight shoes before tissue swelling begins.
CLEAN & BANDAGE: Clean wound gently with soap and water. Wrap a firm, broad pressure bandage over bite site and upward along limb (snug like a sprain wrap, not cutting arterial pulse).
TRANSPORT: Carry or transport victim immediately to government anti-venom hospital (Government Royapettah or Saidapet Multi-Specialty).
warnings: DO NOT cut the wound with a blade.
DO NOT attempt to suck venom with your mouth.
DO NOT apply ice or tight arterial tourniquets.
